strings.name: Peter Wennink
strings.role: Business executive, HEINEKEN supervisory chair and former ASML CEO
strings.summary: Wennink moved from accounting and auditing into semiconductor equipment management, first as ASML’s finance chief and later as CEO, working with its technical leadership on expansion and advanced lithography. After retiring in 2024, he turned to corporate supervision and investment advice; he chairs HEINEKEN’s Supervisory Board.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Through ASML management and lithography commercialization, he helped develop advanced chipmaking equipment within the global semiconductor supply chain.
strings.facts.f1.label: Professional foundation
strings.facts.f1.value: Audit and consulting at Deloitte, later as a partner specializing in high-technology businesses.
strings.facts.f2.label: Training
strings.facts.f2.value: Professional accounting and auditing training through NIVRA; a registered-accountant background.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Connecting finance with industrial technology
strings.highlights.h1.text: He advanced from ASML finance chief to CEO, working with engineers, customers and suppliers to build advanced lithography operations.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Contributing to Dutch investment policy
strings.highlights.h2.text: After retirement he proposed national investment and innovation measures, stressing infrastructure, talent and execution; proposals are not completed investments.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Overseeing HEINEKEN leadership succession
strings.timeline.t1.text: As supervisory chair he discussed the CEO selection process and continuity; supervision differs from day-to-day executive management.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Publishing the Wennink Report
strings.timeline.t2.text: His Dutch prosperity advice identified four strategic domains and roughly €126 billion in investment potential, envisaged largely from private funding.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Becoming HEINEKEN supervisory chair
strings.timeline.t3.text: After previously joining its Supervisory Board, he became chair, responsible for oversight of management.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Retiring from ASML
strings.timeline.t4.text: He ended his presidency and CEO tenure, succeeded by Christophe Fouquet; longstanding technology partner Martin van den Brink retired simultaneously.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Becoming ASML president and CEO
strings.timeline.t5.text: He moved from finance to overall management, co-leading the equipment maker with its technical leadership.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joining ASML management
strings.timeline.t6.text: He became executive vice president, CFO and management board member, bringing audit and industrial-client experience.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Becoming a Deloitte partner
strings.timeline.t7.text: Following years in audit and consulting, he became a partner and developed financial and managerial expertise in high technology.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Beginning an accounting career
strings.timeline.t8.text: He entered varied accounting and audit roles within Deloitte, laying foundations for later corporate finance leadership.
